title: Local Craig interpolation is equivalent to preservation of weak pullbacks by the forgetful functor
author: Matteo De Berardinis and Silvio Ghilardi
work: A Proof Theory for Profinite Modal Algebras
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 12 of the article (source label thm:craig, source0.tex lines 2278--2280), the categorical characterization of the Local Craig Interpolation Theorem, delivered with the author's own complete 42-line proof at source0.tex lines 2282--2323. H2: the proof is not a routine duality chase. The solver must first reduce superamalgamation of a commutative square of profinite modal algebras to the superamalgamation property of all weak pushouts, then dualize the square to locally finite Kripke frames and translate the (SAP) condition into a quantified inclusion between inverse images, use the fact that inverse image along a map of frames has both a left and a right adjoint to eliminate the universally quantified subset, reduce the resulting inclusion to singleton subsets, and finally recognize the surviving condition as exactly the weak-pullback condition for the dual square in the category of sets. Each step is a genuine categorical manipulation of the profinite duality rather than a qualifying examination exercise.
